_comment: UI-hints sidecar for the onboarding intake form (ADR 1061). PRESENTATION ONLY — field grouping, labels, plain-English help, and tier presets. Enums / required-ness / patterns are sourced live from the canonical schema (GET /api/onboard/schema) via each field's enumFrom/schemaPath, so dropdowns can never drift from what the linter enforces. The schema is the source of truth; this file makes it human-friendly.

tiers.label: Developer — dev access + fabric pub/sub
tiers.help: Web surfaces AND a Zenoh per-uuid slot to publish/subscribe on the fabric. NOT backend admin. This is the common 'engineer' tier.

tiers.label: Browse — web surfaces only
tiers.help: Read-only web surfaces (panoscope / portal / stethoscope / flashlight) via Ory login. No fabric cert, no pub/sub.

tiers.label: IAM Admin — identity/access + security monitoring
tiers.help: Manages identity/access across NetBird, Ory, and Zenoh ACLs (provision / rotate / revoke / edit accounts) AND reads security diagnostics (anomaly / flood / usage — a second set of eyes). NOT a full platform admin, and NOT a developer (no Zenoh dev cert). Mesh role is MONITOR; the actual mutate power comes from operator-roster credentials granted out-of-band (see the admin-operator guide). See onboard-tier-role-model.md.

tiers.label: Platform Admin — backend admin + fabric test
tiers.help: Full backend super-user: mgmt server, ACLs, all consoles (Ory ADMINS). PLUS developer fabric access — its own Zenoh slot — so an admin can publish/subscribe to test and troubleshoot the fabric. This is the grammar's ADMIN + DEVELOPER composition. Use sparingly. (The IAM-mutate credentials are still granted out-of-band.)

sections.title: Identity — the person or system
sections.help: Who is being onboarded. The handle is the login, the manifest filename, and the on-wire anchor — pick it carefully; it is kebab-case and unique.

fields.label: Handle
fields.help: Lowercase kebab-case, 3–32 chars (e.g. jane-doe). Becomes the login, the <handle>.yml filename, and the cert anchor.

fields.label: Email
fields.help: The Ory/Kratos login identifier. Also the de-dup key — a second onboarding with the same email is a collision, not a new person.

fields.label: Display name
fields.help: The person's (or system's) human-readable name. UTF-8 / diacritics are fine.

fields.label: Principal type

enumLabels.system: system — a machine / service / autonomous asset

fields.help: person = a human; system = a machine/service/autonomous asset.

fields.label: Your email (you, the submitter)
fields.help: YOUR email — not the person being onboarded (that's 'Email' above). Recorded as who provisioned this onboarding. This is the same 'you' shown as Sponsor at the bottom; the schema needs it as an email, the queue records it as your login handle.

sections.title: Affiliation — who they belong to
sections.help: Orthogonal to capability (ADR 1043): WHO the principal belongs to, never WHAT they may do. Required for onboardings on/after the grammar cutover. A whole unit/cohort shares one slug.

fields.label: Unit slug
fields.help: Stable kebab-case slug shared across everyone in the unit (e.g. demo-org, example-unit).

fields.label: Sector

enumLabels.state: state — government (armed forces, a ministry, police, a state lab)

fields.help: What your organization is. If it sells what it does, pick commercial, even if a government owns it. This does not ask whether you are foreign — that comes from your nation.

fields.label: Branch
fields.help: Only if you picked state above.

fields.label: Nation
fields.help: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (e.g. POL, USA, DEU) or a multinational tag (NATO, EU). Optional but recommended.

fields.label: Unit display name
fields.help: Human-readable unit name (e.g. "Example National Forces").

fields.label: Unit code scheme
fields.help: Only for organic (this sovereign's own) + partner (foreign / multinational) units with a codified unit ID. Leave unset otherwise. This is mutable — it can change on reorg/comrel and is updatable later.

fields.label: Unit code value
fields.help: The code itself (e.g. a 6-char US UIC). Required if a scheme is chosen.

fields.label: Unit code effective date
fields.help: Optional YYYY-MM-DD the code took effect. Leave blank if unknown.

fields.label: Unit code source

enumLabels.open-source: open-source — from an open ORBAT source

fields.help: How this code was verified. Set by the unit-reference match; leave blank (= self-asserted) if entered by hand.

sections.title: Organization (attribution)
sections.help: Org label carried in the portal + surfaces. For a commercial vendor this is the company; for a partner unit it can mirror the affiliation display name. (Schema key is 'vendor' until ADR 1052 renames it; shown here as Organization.)

fields.label: Organization
fields.help: Org/company name shown on the surfaces. Required for the developer tier.

sections.title: Access tier + mesh
sections.help: Pick a tier (it sets the mesh groups + fabric cert). Site is which goatnet they join.

fields.label: Tier
fields.help: Choose the access level; the form fills the mesh groups + Zenoh accordingly. You can still tweak the advanced fields below.

fields.label: Site(s)
fields.help: Which goatnet(s) the peer enrolls in (e.g. galaxy). Usually one.

fields.label: Mesh role
fields.help: Almost always 'peer'. bootstrap/admin/operator carry shorter default key TTLs. (This is the NetBird setup-key role, not the access tier.)

fields.label: Setup-key reuse
fields.help: How many machines one bundle can enroll (1–100). 5 is the cohort default.

fields.label: May sponsor others
fields.help: Decided at onboarding (ADR 1071): may this person mint candidate-onboarding invites and vouch for submissions? The IAM Admin / Platform Admin tiers set it automatically; for anyone else it is a deliberate case-by-case grant. Revocable later via `goat admin sponsorship --revoke`.

fields.label: Max sponsorable tier
fields.help: The highest tier this person may sponsor — at most their OWN tier, never above it. Required when 'May sponsor others' is on (an authorized identity with no recorded cap fails closed to the lowest tier).

advanced.title: Advanced — raw groups + Zenoh (set by the tier; edit only if you know why)

fields.label: NetBird groups
fields.help: Mesh role + node-class groups. Capability is named by ROLE here (DEVELOPER/OPERATOR/OBSERVER…), never by affiliation. Deprecated tokens (VENDOR/OFFSITE) are rejected post-cutover.

fields.label: Zenoh fabric cert
fields.help: On = the principal gets a per-uuid slot to publish/subscribe. Off = web surfaces only.

fields.label: Zenoh anchor prefix
fields.help: URI-SAN prefix recorded for the cert (the portal assigns the real uuid slot). Defaults to the handle.

sponsor.label: Sponsor = you
sponsor.help: This is YOU — your login handle, bound automatically when the proposal is stored (you vouch for this onboarding). Same person as 'Your email' above, just the handle the queue shows. Not editable, can't be forged.
